short_description.id: Luupainaja adalah roh dalam mitologi Estonia yang menindih orang dan hewan yang sedang tidur pada malam hari, dan bisa diusir dengan menggerakkan ibu jari kaki atau menyalakan api.
short_description.en: The luupainaja is a spirit of Estonian mythology that presses on sleeping people and animals at night and can be driven off by moving the big toe or lighting a fire.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Estonia, luupainaja, yang juga disebut painaja, painak, atau tallaja, adalah roh yang menindih orang yang sedang tidur. Ia datang pada malam hari dan menekan tubuh korban sehingga korban tidak bisa bergerak. Orang tua dahulu percaya tindihan yang lama bisa membawa kematian, dan luupainaja juga menindih hewan pekerja untuk melemahkan tenaganya.
long_description.en: In Estonian mythology the luupainaja, also called painaja, painak or tallaja, is a spirit that presses down on sleepers. It comes at night and weighs on the victim's body so that they cannot move. The old folk believed prolonged pressing could kill, and the luupainaja also pressed on working animals to sap their strength.

long_description.id: Dalam kebanyakan cerita ia tampak sebagai perempuan muda, tetapi juga sebagai perempuan atau lelaki tua, atau sebagai kucing hitam, kuda, dan anjing. Untuk melepaskan diri, orang menggerakkan ibu jari kaki atau menyalakan api, karena luupainaja takut cahaya.
long_description.en: In most tales it appears as a young woman, but also as an old woman or old man, or as a black cat, horse or dog. To get free, people moved their big toe or lit a fire, since the luupainaja fears light.

long_description.id: M. J. Eisen mencatat bahwa luupainaja memilih korban dan menindihnya setiap malam seperti batu di dada. Menurut kisah yang dikenal luas, bila lubang masuknya ditutup dan api dinyalakan, ia tampak sebagai gadis muda yang kemudian dinikahi korbannya, sampai suaminya mencabut sumbat lubang itu dan sang istri lenyap. Eisen menyimpulkan bahwa luupainaja sebenarnya penyihir, manusia yang jiwanya meninggalkan tubuh dan mengambil berbagai wujud.
long_description.en: M. J. Eisen recorded that the luupainaja chooses a victim and presses on them nightly like a stone on the chest. In a widely known tale, when its entry hole is stopped and a light is struck it appears as a young girl whom the victim marries, until the husband pulls the plug from the hole and the wife vanishes. Eisen concluded that the luupainaja is really a witch, a human whose soul leaves the body and takes various forms.

claims.quote: Luupainaja on eesti mütoloogias magajaid painav vaim.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Estonia, luupainaja adalah roh yang menindih orang yang sedang tidur.
statement.en: In Estonian mythology the luupainaja is a spirit that presses down on sleepers.

claims.quote: Luupainaja teiste nimetuste hulka kuuluvad painaja, painak, panijas, paanjas, painakane, luupaanija, luupaine, luupatak, tallaja.

statement.id: Nama lain luupainaja antara lain painaja, painak, panijas, paanjas, painakane, luupaanija, luupaine, luupatak, dan tallaja.
statement.en: Other names of the luupainaja include painaja, painak, panijas, paanjas, painakane, luupaanija, luupaine, luupatak and tallaja.

claims.quote: Nimelt käivad tallajad öösiti oma ohvrit painamas. Nad rõhuvad oma ohvri keha, nii et too liigutada ei saa.

statement.id: Tallaja datang pada malam hari menindih korbannya, menekan tubuh korban sehingga ia tidak bisa bergerak.
statement.en: The tallajad come at night to press on their victim, weighing down the body so the victim cannot move.

claims.quote: Vanarahvas arvas, et pikaaegne painamine võib surma tuua. Tallajad ei käi ainult inimesi piinamas, vaid üritavad ka tööloomade jõudu oma rõhumisega nõrgendada.

statement.id: Orang tua dahulu percaya bahwa tindihan yang berlangsung lama bisa membawa kematian; tallaja tidak hanya menyiksa manusia tetapi juga berusaha melemahkan tenaga hewan pekerja dengan tindihannya.
statement.en: The old folk believed prolonged pressing could bring death; the tallajad torment not only people but also try to weaken working animals by pressing on them.

claims.quote: Enamikus juttudes on öeldud, et tallajad ilmutavad end noore naisena, kuid ei pelga ära ka vana naise ja vana mehena ilmumist. Samuti on loomadega – luupainajaid kirjeldatakse nii mustade kassidena, hobustena, koertena jne.

statement.id: Dalam kebanyakan cerita, tallaja menampakkan diri sebagai perempuan muda, tetapi juga sebagai perempuan tua atau lelaki tua; luupainaja juga digambarkan sebagai kucing hitam, kuda, anjing, dan sebagainya.
statement.en: In most tales the tallajad appear as a young woman, though also as an old woman or old man; luupainajad are also described as black cats, horses, dogs and so on.

claims.quote: Lihtsaim neist on suure varba liigutamine. Nimelt arvati, et kui tunned luupainajat end rõhuvat, tuleb suurt varvast liigutada ning siis tallaja põgeneb.

statement.id: Cara paling mudah untuk melepaskan diri adalah menggerakkan ibu jari kaki: orang percaya bila merasa ditindih luupainaja, ibu jari kaki harus digerakkan, maka tallaja akan lari.
statement.en: The simplest way to get free is to move the big toe: it was believed that if you feel the luupainaja pressing on you, you must move your big toe and the tallaja will flee.

claims.quote: Teiseks levinud võimaluseks oli tule põlema panemine, valgust pidavat luupainajad kartma.

statement.id: Cara umum lainnya adalah menyalakan api, karena luupainaja konon takut cahaya.
statement.en: Another common way was to light a fire, as the luupainajad were said to fear light.

claims.quote: Luupainaja valib enesele mingisuguse isiku ohvriks ja hakkab seda kas igal ööl ehk mõne öö takka painamas käima, nagu kivi rinnul ehk kehal lasudes

statement.id: Menurut M. J. Eisen, luupainaja memilih seseorang sebagai korban dan datang menindihnya setiap malam atau selang beberapa malam, seperti batu yang menimpa dada atau tubuh.
statement.en: According to M. J. Eisen, the luupainaja chooses a person as its victim and comes to press on them every night or every few nights, lying like a stone on the chest or body.

claims.quote: Laialt tuntakse lugu, mille järele sissetuleku-augu sulgumise ja tulesüütamise peale luupainaja ilmub noorena tütarlapsena, kelle painatav hiljemini enesele kosib.

statement.id: Dikenal luas kisah bahwa bila lubang masuknya ditutup dan api dinyalakan, luupainaja menampakkan diri sebagai gadis muda, yang kemudian dilamar oleh orang yang ditindihnya.
statement.en: A widely known tale says that when its entry hole is closed and a light is struck, the luupainaja appears as a young girl, whom the person she pressed later marries.

claims.quote: Mõlemad elavad õnnelikult, kuni abielumees 7 ehk 14 aastat pärast pulmi luupainaja sissetuleku-augu eest pulga võtab, ja kohe kaob naine nagu õhk toast.

statement.id: Keduanya hidup bahagia sampai sang suami, 7 atau 14 tahun setelah pernikahan, mencabut sumbat dari lubang masuk luupainaja, dan seketika sang istri lenyap dari ruangan seperti udara.
statement.en: Both live happily until the husband, 7 or 14 years after the wedding, pulls the plug from the luupainaja's entry hole, and at once the wife vanishes from the room like air.

claims.quote: Nagu eelmistest seletustest selgub, on luupainaja inimene, kuid mitte tavaline inimene, vaid niisugune, kes enesele iseäraliku tarkusega vaimude omaduse pärinud, teise sõnaga nõid.

statement.id: Eisen menyimpulkan bahwa luupainaja adalah manusia, tetapi bukan manusia biasa, melainkan orang yang dengan pengetahuan khusus memperoleh sifat roh, dengan kata lain seorang penyihir.
statement.en: Eisen concludes that the luupainaja is a human, but not an ordinary one: someone who by special knowledge has acquired the qualities of spirits, in other words a witch.

claims.quote: Tõepoolest ei muuda luupainaja inimlik keha ennast sugugi, vaid hing lahkub kehast, enesele lahkudes üht ehk teist kuju võttes.

statement.id: Tubuh manusia luupainaja sebenarnya tidak berubah; jiwanya yang meninggalkan tubuh dan mengambil satu atau lain wujud.
statement.en: The luupainaja's human body does not really change; rather the soul leaves the body, taking one form or another as it goes.

summary.en: A spirit that presses on sleepers.

summary.id: Penyihir manusia yang jiwanya meninggalkan tubuh (Eisen).
summary.en: A human witch whose soul leaves the body (Eisen).

short_description.id: Nihang adalah naga air bersurai emas dalam mitologi Chitrali di Pakistan barat laut. Kisah terkenalnya menceritakan naga danau di Mastuj yang dibunuh seorang pemberani dengan pedang beracun bergagang ganda.
short_description.en: The Nihang is a golden-maned water dragon of Chitrali mythology in northwestern Pakistan. Its best-known tale tells of a lake dragon at Mastuj slain by a brave man with a poisoned, double-hilted sword.

long_description.id: Nihang adalah naga air dalam mitologi Chitrali di Pakistan barat laut. Namanya diturunkan dari kata Persia nahang, yang berarti buaya tetapi juga dipakai untuk aneka makhluk laut. Makhluk ini dibayangkan sebagai ular bersayap yang sangat besar, bersisik, dan bersurai emas.
long_description.en: The Nihang is a water dragon of Chitrali mythology in northwestern Pakistan. Its name comes from the Persian word nahang, meaning crocodile but also applied to assorted sea creatures. It is imagined as a very large, scaly winged serpent with a golden mane.

long_description.id: Menurut artikel kedua, ciri tubuhnya mengingatkan pada naga Asia Timur: surai tebal seperti bulu, hidup di air, dan badan panjang ramping menyerupai ular. Bedanya, Nihang dipandang sebagai makhluk jahat yang menebar teror di sekitarnya. Penulis yang sama menilai kepercayaan pada makhluk penghuni danau sudah tua di pegunungan Hindu Kush.
long_description.en: According to the second source, its body recalls East Asian dragons: a thick fur-like mane, a watery home and a long slender snake-like body. Unlike them, however, the Nihang is seen as a malevolent creature spreading terror around it. The same author considers belief in lake-dwelling beings to be old in the Hindu Kush mountains.

long_description.id: Kisah paling terkenal terjadi di Mastuj. Dahulu sungai di sana membentuk danau besar di bawah kota, tempat seekor naga raksasa memangsa ikan, hewan, dan akhirnya manusia. Naga itu kebal senjata dan panah tidak dapat menjangkaunya dari jauh.
long_description.en: The best-known tale is set in Mastuj. Long ago the river there formed a large lake below the town, where a giant dragon preyed on fish, animals and eventually people. It could not be harmed by weapons, and arrows could not reach it from afar.

long_description.id: Seorang pemberani lalu memesan pedang panjang bergagang di kedua ujung dan melumuri matanya dengan racun. Saat naga menyedotnya ke dalam mulut, bilah itu membelah rahangnya dan racun menyelesaikan sisanya. Ia membawa pulang seikat rambut emas dari surai naga ke istana. Danau itu kini lenyap, tetapi tempatnya masih bernama Nahangu Chhat, yang dalam bahasa Khowar berarti Danau Naga.
long_description.en: A brave man then had a long sword made with a hilt at each end and poisoned its edge. When the dragon drew him into its mouth, the blade split its jaws and the poison did the rest. He carried a golden lock of the dragon's mane back to the palace. The lake has since vanished, yet the spot is still named Nahangu Chhat, meaning The Dragon's Lake in Khowar.

literal_meaning.id: buaya; juga dipakai untuk berbagai makhluk laut
literal_meaning.en: crocodile; also used for various sea creatures

who.id: Nihang adalah naga air bersurai emas dalam mitologi Chitrali.
who.en: The Nihang is a golden-maned water dragon of Chitrali mythology.

origin.id: Ia berasal dari tradisi Chitrali di Pakistan barat laut.
origin.en: It comes from the Chitrali tradition of northwestern Pakistan.

role.id: Dalam kisah, ia meneror penduduk di sekitar danau tempat tinggalnya.
role.en: In the tales it terrorizes the people living around its lake.

famous_for.id: Ia terkenal karena naga danau Mastuj yang dibunuh dengan pedang beracun bergagang ganda.
famous_for.en: It is famous for the Mastuj lake dragon slain with a poisoned double-hilted sword.

did_you_know.id: Danau tempat naga Mastuj tinggal sudah hilang, tetapi lokasinya masih dinamai Nahangu Chhat, Danau Naga.
did_you_know.en: The lake of the Mastuj dragon is gone, but the site is still named Nahangu Chhat, The Dragon's Lake.

description.id: Naga Mastuj kebal senjata biasa, tetapi tewas ketika pedang beracun bergagang di kedua ujung membelah rahangnya.
description.en: The Mastuj dragon resisted ordinary weapons but died when a poisoned sword hilted at both ends split its jaws.

role.id: Naga pemangsa yang menghuni danau di bawah kota.
role.en: The predatory dragon living in the lake below the town.

summary.id: Naga di danau Mastuj memangsa ikan, hewan, lalu manusia. Seorang pemberani memesan pedang bergagang ganda, meracuni bilahnya, dan membunuh naga itu saat disedot ke mulutnya; ia membawa seikat rambut emas surainya ke istana.
summary.en: The dragon of the Mastuj lake preyed on fish, animals and then people. A brave man had a double-hilted sword made, poisoned its blade and killed the dragon as it sucked him into its mouth; he brought a golden lock of its mane to the palace.

description.id: Bekas danau di bawah kota Mastuj tempat naga itu tinggal; danaunya sudah tidak ada, tetapi namanya bertahan.
description.en: Former lake below the town of Mastuj where the dragon lived; the lake is gone but the name survives.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa nama sebuah tempat bisa menyimpan ingatan tentang makhluk mitos walaupun danaunya sudah hilang?
learning_questions.en: Why might a place name keep the memory of a mythical creature even after the lake itself has disappeared?

sources.title: Dragon Lake Saga - A Chitrali Myth
sources.author: Faheem Ahmad Khan
sources.publisher: Mahraka.com (website on the culture, history and languages of Chitral)

claims.quote: Nihang are mythical water dragons from the Chitrali mythology in northwestern Pakistan.

statement.id: Nihang adalah naga air mitos (mythical water dragons) dalam mitologi Chitrali di Pakistan barat laut.
statement.en: Nihang are mythical water dragons from the Chitrali mythology in northwestern Pakistan.

claims.quote: Other creatures of fame in Chitrali Mythology are the lake-dwelling dragons, known as Nihang, the name being derived from the Persian word nahang for crocodiles but classically used for various sea creatures.

statement.id: Naga penghuni danau (lake-dwelling dragons) dalam mitologi Chitrali disebut Nihang; namanya berasal dari kata Persia nahang untuk buaya, yang secara klasik juga dipakai untuk berbagai makhluk laut.
statement.en: The lake-dwelling dragons of Chitrali mythology are called Nihang; the name derives from the Persian word nahang for crocodiles, classically also used for various sea creatures.

claims.quote: Perhaps a better term for these creatures would be winged serpents, also found in many parts of mainland Pakistan. These gigantic scaly creatures were known for their golden manes,

statement.id: Penulis menilai makhluk ini lebih tepat disebut ular bersayap (winged serpents); mereka raksasa bersisik yang dikenal karena surai emasnya (golden manes).
statement.en: The author suggests these creatures are better called winged serpents; they were gigantic scaly creatures known for their golden manes.

claims.quote: one of them inhabited a lake in Chitral where it terrorized the local populace, but its reign of terror ended when one day an ancient warrior stood up against it using a double-hilted sword.

statement.id: Salah satunya menghuni sebuah danau di Chitral dan meneror penduduk, sampai seorang pendekar kuno melawannya dengan pedang bergagang ganda (double-hilted sword).
statement.en: One of them inhabited a lake in Chitral and terrorized the populace until an ancient warrior stood up against it with a double-hilted sword.

claims.quote: the physical description of the dragon appears to be completely East Asian with the thick furlike mane, aquatic habitat, and a long slender serpent-like body, however, unlike the Eastern dragons, the Chitrali dragon appears to be a malevolent creature bent on keeping a reign of terror upon its vicinity.

statement.id: Wujud naga Chitrali tampak sepenuhnya Asia Timur (East Asian): surai tebal seperti bulu, habitat air, dan tubuh panjang ramping seperti ular; namun tidak seperti naga Timur, ia makhluk jahat (malevolent) yang meneror sekitarnya.
statement.en: The Chitrali dragon looks wholly East Asian, with a thick fur-like mane, aquatic habitat and long slender serpent-like body, but unlike Eastern dragons it is a malevolent creature that terrorizes its vicinity.

claims.quote: Lake dwelling creatures seem to be an ancient belief of the Hindu Kush mountains.

statement.id: Makhluk penghuni danau tampaknya merupakan kepercayaan kuno di pegunungan Hindu Kush (Hindu Kush mountains).
statement.en: Lake-dwelling creatures seem to be an ancient belief of the Hindu Kush mountains.

claims.quote: The river which flows by Mastuj, once formed a large lake just below the town. It is said that an enormous dragon lived in the lake. He preyed upon all living things, ranging from fish to animals. With the passage of time, he began to attack humans.

statement.id: Sungai yang mengalir di dekat Mastuj dulu membentuk danau besar di bawah kota; konon seekor naga raksasa (enormous dragon) tinggal di sana, memangsa segala makhluk hidup dari ikan hingga hewan, lalu mulai menyerang manusia.
statement.en: The river by Mastuj once formed a large lake below the town; an enormous dragon is said to have lived there, preying on all living things from fish to animals, and later began to attack humans.

claims.quote: The huge reptile was invulnerable to weapons. Arrows didn’t reach him from a long distance, while going near it was difficult and risky.

statement.id: Reptil raksasa itu kebal senjata (invulnerable to weapons); anak panah tidak mencapainya dari jauh, sedangkan mendekatinya sulit dan berbahaya.
statement.en: The huge reptile was invulnerable to weapons; arrows did not reach it from afar, and approaching it was difficult and risky.

claims.quote: Afterwards he ordered a blacksmith to make a long and sharp sword, with a hilt on both ends.

statement.id: Sang pemberani memesan kepada pandai besi (blacksmith) sebilah pedang panjang dan tajam dengan gagang di kedua ujungnya.
statement.en: The brave man had a blacksmith make a long sharp sword with a hilt on both ends.

claims.quote: As soon as he pulled the man towards its mouth, the razor sharp blade of the sword began slicing his jaws apart. Soon he went down to its belly, poison swiftly completed the rest of the job.

statement.id: Ketika naga menyedot sang pria ke mulutnya, bilah pedang yang sangat tajam membelah rahangnya (jaws), dan racun (poison) menuntaskan sisanya.
statement.en: When the dragon pulled the man towards its mouth, the razor-sharp blade sliced its jaws apart, and poison finished the job.

claims.quote: The brave man cut one of the golden locks from the dragon’s mane and galloped his horse towards the royal court.

statement.id: Sang pemberani memotong seikat rambut emas (golden locks) dari surai naga lalu memacu kudanya ke istana raja.
statement.en: The brave man cut one of the golden locks from the dragon's mane and rode to the royal court.

claims.quote: The Lake no more exists today but the place is still called Nahangu Chhat (The Dragon’s Lake).

statement.id: Danau itu kini sudah tidak ada, tetapi tempatnya masih disebut Nahangu Chhat (The Dragon's Lake, Danau Naga).
statement.en: The lake no longer exists, but the place is still called Nahangu Chhat (The Dragon's Lake).

claims.quote: Though the lake is gone, the place is still called Nahangu Chhat, which means "The Dragon’s Lake" in the Khowar language.

statement.id: Nama tempat Nahangu Chhat berarti Danau Naga (The Dragon's Lake) dalam bahasa Khowar.
statement.en: The place name Nahangu Chhat means The Dragon's Lake in the Khowar language.

short_description.id: Hippogryph (Pferdegreif dalam heraldik) adalah makhluk dongeng campuran, separuh griffin dan separuh kuda, yang muncul dalam epos kesatria Italia.
short_description.en: The hippogryph (Pferdegreif in heraldry) is a fabulous hybrid, half griffin and half horse, that appears in Italian chivalric epics.

long_description.id: Hippogryph (dari bahasa Italia ippogrifo, gabungan hippos, "kuda", dan kata Italia grifo, "griffin") adalah makhluk dongeng campuran yang separuh griffin dan separuh kuda. Menurut artikel de, istilah ini adalah ciptaan Matteo Maria Boiardo, yang menampilkan makhluk yang luar biasa cepat ini pada 1486 dalam L'Orlando Innamorato; pada 1532 Ariost mengambilnya ke dalam epos lanjutan Der rasende Roland. Artikel en justru menyebut makhluk ini ciptaan Ludovico Ariosto dalam Orlando Furioso pada awal abad ke-16, dengan bagian depan elang dan bagian belakang kuda.
long_description.en: The hippogryph (from Italian ippogrifo, combining hippos, "horse", and Italian grifo, "griffin") is a fabulous hybrid that is half griffin and half horse. According to the de article, the term was invented by Matteo Maria Boiardo, who featured this astonishingly fast creature in 1486 in L'Orlando Innamorato; in 1532 Ariost took it into his sequel epic Der rasende Roland. The en article instead credits Ludovico Ariosto's Orlando Furioso, early in the 16th century, picturing an eagle in front and a horse behind.

long_description.id: Gagasan makhluk ini berasal dari ungkapan terpelajar bahwa persilangan griffin dan kuda adalah hal yang mustahil; Boiardo kemungkinan terilhami Eclogae karya Vergil, yang memakai perkawinan semacam itu sebagai kiasan pernikahan yang absurd. Dalam syair Ariosto, hippogryph lahir dari kuda betina dan griffin, sangat cepat, dan dapat terbang mengelilingi dunia hingga ke Bulan. Roger (Ruggiero) menyelamatkan putri Angelica dari monster laut dengan menungganginya, dan Astolfo terbang ke Bulan untuk mencari akal Roland yang hilang.
long_description.en: The idea comes from a learned saying that crossing a griffin with a horse is impossible; Boiardo was probably inspired by Vergil's Eclogae, which use such a pairing as a metaphor for an absurd marriage. In Ariosto's poem the hippogryph is born of a mare and a griffin, is extremely fast, and can fly around the world and to the Moon. Roger (Ruggiero) rescues princess Angelica from a sea monster riding it, and Astolfo flies to the Moon to find Roland's lost wits.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah-kisah kemudian, misalnya Oberon karya Christoph Martin Wieland, hippogryph sering menjadi sinonim Pegasus. Ia juga muncul dalam fantasi modern seperti Dungeons & Dragons dan seri Harry Potter, dengan hippogreif Seidenschnabel yang berperan penting dalam buku ketiga. Dalam heraldik, motif ini dikenal sebagai Pferdegreif.
long_description.en: In later tales, such as Christoph Martin Wieland's Oberon, the hippogryph often stands for Pegasus. It also appears in modern fantasy such as Dungeons & Dragons and the Harry Potter series, where the hippogreif Seidenschnabel plays a key role in the third book. In heraldry the motif is known as the Pferdegreif.

short_description.id: Black Dog of Newgate adalah legenda hantu anjing hitam raksasa yang menghantui bekas Penjara Newgate, London, dan dikaitkan dengan kisah penyihir yang dibunuh narapidana saat kelaparan.
short_description.en: The Black Dog of Newgate is a legend of a monstrous black dog haunting the former Newgate Prison in London, tied to the story of a sorcerer killed by inmates during a famine.

long_description.id: Black Dog of Newgate adalah legenda tentang hantu di bekas Penjara Newgate, London, yang terletak di sebelah Old Bailey. Kisah ini contoh kategori Black Dog Inggris, yaitu anjing pemburu hantu pertanda buruk atau berniat jahat. Catatan tertuanya berasal dari 1596 dan dikreditkan kepada narapidana bernama Luke Hutton.
long_description.en: The Black Dog of Newgate is a legend about a haunting at the former Newgate Prison in London, which stood beside the Old Bailey. It is an example of the English Black Dog type, a spectral hound of ill omen or malicious intent. The earliest recorded account dates from 1596 and is credited to an inmate named Luke Hutton.

long_description.id: Dalam ceritanya, saat kelaparan pada masa Raja Henry III dari Inggris, seorang cendekiawan yang dikenal sebagai penyihir dipenjara di Newgate. Para narapidana, yang sudah beralih ke kanibalisme, memakannya. Tak lama kemudian mereka konon melihat anjing hitam raksasa yang dianggap arwah sang penyihir; ia membunuh dan memakan para pelaku satu per satu sampai penyintas terakhir kabur dari penjara.
long_description.en: The tale is set during a famine under England's King Henry III, when a scholar reputed to be a sorcerer was locked up in Newgate. The prisoners, who had already turned to cannibalism, ate him. Soon afterwards they reportedly saw a monstrous black dog taken to be the sorcerer's spirit; it killed and ate those responsible one by one until the last survivors broke out of the prison.

long_description.id: Menjelang akhir narasi, orang asing tak bernama itu mengaku kisah anjing roh tidak benar dan satu-satunya Black Dog yang ia dengar adalah batu hitam besar di ruang bawah tanah. Kisah ini dimaksudkan sebagai cerita moral melawan hidup nista para narapidana.
long_description.en: Towards the end of the narrative the unnamed stranger says the spirit-dog tale is untrue and the only Black Dog he has heard of is a great black stone in the dungeon. The story was meant as a morality tale against the base living of the inmates.

long_description.id: Ada spekulasi bahwa hantu ini berkaitan dengan Amen Court di dekatnya. Menurut sumber kedua, hantunya muncul sebagai bentuk hitam tak berbentuk yang menyelinap di sepanjang dinding dan mengeluarkan bau menjijikkan, disertai bunyi langkah diseret.
long_description.en: There is speculation that the haunting is linked with nearby Amen Court. The second source reports a ghost in the form of a formless black shape that creeps along walls, gives off a foul smell, and is accompanied by the sound of dragging footsteps.

short_description.id: Çarşamba Karısı adalah sosok perempuan menakutkan dalam kepercayaan rakyat di Azerbaijan dan Anadolu, yang marah dan membawa celaka ke rumah tempat orang bekerja pada malam Rabu atau membiarkan pekerjaan tak selesai.
short_description.en: Çarşamba Karısı is a frightening female figure of folk belief in Azerbaijan and Anadolu who grows angry and brings harm to houses where people work on Wednesday night or leave work unfinished.

long_description.id: Di Azerbaijan dan sebagian daerah Anadolu, Çarşamba Karısı (juga Çarşamba Avradı) dibayangkan sebagai perempuan buruk rupa, berpakaian jelek, dan menakutkan. Ia marah bila ada pekerjaan dilakukan pada malam Rabu, lalu mendatangkan keburukan pada rumah tersebut.
long_description.en: In Azerbaijan and parts of Anadolu, Çarşamba Karısı (also Çarşamba Avradı) is imagined as an ugly, poorly dressed and frightening woman. She becomes angry when work is done on Wednesday night and then brings misfortune upon that household.

long_description.id: Pada hari Rabu ia disebut masuk ke rumah-rumah yang masih menyimpan pekerjaan belum rampung dan membuat semuanya kacau, serta mencelakai penghuninya. Ia tidak gentar kepada siapa pun dan membawa pergi anak-anak secara terang-terangan di hadapan semua orang, bukan sembunyi-sembunyi.
long_description.en: On Wednesdays she is said to enter houses where work is left unfinished, throw everything into confusion and harm the occupants. She fears nobody and takes children away openly in front of everyone rather than in secret.

long_description.id: Kedua sumber mengaitkannya dengan Alkarısı, dan artikel pertama memandangnya lebih sebagai unsur memorat sejenis hantu, jin, peri, atau momok ketimbang makhluk mitologis. Dalam bahasa sehari-hari, ungkapan Çarşamba Karısı juga dipakai secara kiasan untuk perempuan yang rambut dan pakaiannya acak-acakan.
long_description.en: Both sources link her with Alkarısı, and the first article regards her more as a memorate element akin to ghosts, jinn, fairies or bogeys than as a mythological creature. In everyday speech, the expression Çarşamba Karısı is also used figuratively for a woman whose hair and clothes are in disarray.

claims.quote: Azerbaycan'da ve Anadolu'nun kimi yörelerinde Çarşamba gecesi iş yapılırsa öfkelenen ve o eve kötülük getiren çirkin, kötü giysili, ürkütücü bir kadın olduğu söylenen

statement.id: Di Azerbaijan dan sebagian daerah Anadolu, Çarşamba Karısı disebut sebagai perempuan buruk rupa, berpakaian jelek, dan menakutkan yang marah dan membawa celaka ke rumah bila ada yang bekerja pada malam Rabu (Çarşamba gecesi).
statement.en: In Azerbaijan (Azerbaycan) and some parts of Anadolu, Çarşamba Karısı is said to be an ugly, badly dressed, frightening woman (ürkütücü bir kadın) who grows angry and brings harm to the house (eve kötülük getiren) if work is done on Wednesday night (Çarşamba gecesi).

claims.quote: (Çarşamba Avradı) olarak anılır. Çarşamba günleri bitirilmemiş işler bulunan evlere girerek ortalığı karıştırdığı anlatılır.

statement.id: Ia juga disebut Çarşamba Avradı; konon pada hari Rabu ia masuk ke rumah-rumah yang memiliki pekerjaan belum selesai dan mengacaukan segalanya.
statement.en: It is also called Çarşamba Avradı; it is said to enter houses with unfinished work (bitirilmemiş işler bulunan evlere) on Wednesdays and throw everything into disorder (ortalığı karıştırdığı).

claims.quote: Kimseden korkmaz ve çocukları gizlice değil, herkesin gözü önünde alıp kaçırır.

statement.id: Ia tidak takut kepada siapa pun dan membawa lari anak-anak bukan diam-diam, melainkan di depan mata semua orang.
statement.en: It fears no one (kimseden korkmaz) and carries off children (çocukları alıp kaçırır) not secretly but before everyone's eyes (herkesin gözü önünde).

claims.quote: Türkçe'de mecâzen saçı başı karmakarışık, paspal, özensiz kadın anlamına da gelir.

statement.id: Secara kiasan, dalam bahasa Turki ungkapan ini juga berarti perempuan yang rambutnya kusut dan berpenampilan acak-acakan.
statement.en: Figuratively (mecâzen), in Turkish (Türkçe'de) the expression also means a woman with tangled hair and an untidy, careless appearance (özensiz kadın).

claims.quote: Çarşamba Karısı, Türkçede saçı başı karmakarışık, üstü başı özensiz kadın anlamında kullanılır. Zaman zaman Alkarısı'na tekabül eder.

statement.id: Çarşamba Karısı dipakai untuk menyebut perempuan berambut kusut dan berpakaian acak-acakan; kadang-kadang ia disamakan dengan Alkarısı.
statement.en: Çarşamba Karısı is used (kullanılır) for a woman with tangled hair and careless clothing (özensiz kadın); at times it corresponds to Alkarısı (Alkarısı'na tekabül eder).

claims.quote: Mitolojik bir yaratıktan ziyade hortlak, hayalet, -genel anlamda- cin, peri, öcü, dunganga türünde bir memorat unsurudur.

statement.id: Menurut artikel pertama, Çarşamba Karısı lebih merupakan unsur memorat sejenis hantu, arwah, jin, peri, atau momok daripada makhluk mitologis.
statement.en: According to the first article, Çarşamba Karısı is less a mythological creature (mitolojik bir yaratıktan ziyade) than a memorate element (memorat unsuru) of the type of revenant, ghost (hortlak, hayalet), jinn, fairy or bogey (cin, peri, öcü).

claims.quote: Yine Anadolu inançlarında haftanın belirli bir günü, yarım kalan işlerin olduğu evlere gelerek işleri karıştıran, insanlara kötülük yapan dişi varlık olarak tanımlanır.

statement.id: Dalam kepercayaan Anadolu ia digambarkan sebagai makhluk betina yang pada hari tertentu dalam sepekan datang ke rumah dengan pekerjaan yang belum selesai, mengacaukan pekerjaan itu, dan mencelakai orang.
statement.en: In Anadolu beliefs (Anadolu inançlarında) it is described as a female being (dişi varlık) that on a certain day of the week comes to houses with unfinished work (yarım kalan işlerin olduğu evlere), muddles the work and harms people (insanlara kötülük yapan).

items.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: square premium painterly naturalistic illustration for Mythics folklore encyclopedia. Subject: Çarşamba Karısı, terrifying night hag of Turkish and Azerbaijani folklore. Depict ONE supernatural disheveled hag standing inside the dim interior of a traditional rustic Anatolian stone-and-timber village kitchen at night. She has a haggard, weathered face, wild unkempt tangled grey hair cascading wildly around her shoulders, and a chilling, menacing, furious glare. Dressed in fully modest but untidy, ragged traditional Anatolian rustic clothes: layered patched skirts and a faded coarse shawl. She stands menacingly beside an abandoned spinning wheel with tangled yarn spindles and untidy domestic utensils left unfinished on the wooden table. Atmospheric nocturnal lighting from a single smoking brass oil lamp on the wall, casting deep unsettling shadows across the clay hearth and rough stone walls. Fully clothed, modest framing, no gore, no generic glowing aura, neon outline, energy ribbons or luminous colored mist. Beautifully resolved anatomy, cinematic painterly craft, no text, labels, logo, border, or watermark.
